name: The Dudley Boys

tenures.source: The diary's own shows bill the team on 3 of its first ten shows, from /promotions/ecw-worldwide-nevermore/archive/show-001-p17-21.html.

caption: The tag team that holds the ECW World Tag Team Championship through the diary's first ten shows, beating the Hardy Boys for it on the first and eighth. In March and April 2007 the Dudley Boys, billed as the enforcers of ECW, beat The Sandman on Blood, Sweat and Beers at Tommy Dreamer's booking, are eliminated together by Rhino at Baptism Of Fire, and beat Big Stevie Cool and Hollywood Nova with 3Ds on Blood, Sweat and Beers and Revolution while the Sasuke World Order hunt them. At Cyberslam in April 2007 the Dudley Boys take out Los Guerreros with 3Ds and a Spike Powerbomb through tables in the three-way dance for the tag number one contendership, but the Canadian Connection run in and pin them both; in May D-Von pins Chavo Guerrero Jr. with a 3D. The Dudley Boys return at Wrestlepalooza in June 2007 to attack the Whole F**kin' Show, and in July beat the Hardcore Innovators for the number one contendership with the help of Big Dick Dudley Jr. and Daizy, whom they introduce on Revolution as the children of their missing brother Big Dick Dudley. They lose the Tables Match for the World Tag Team Championship at Summer Assylum, then rename the old World Tag Team belts the Dudleyville Hardcore Titles, keep them over the bWo with the sWo's interference and over Balls & Axl, and are challenged by the Innovators and Los Guerreros. In August 2007 they keep the Dudleyville Hardcore Titles over Los Guerreros (a 3D on Chavo) on Revolution, over the Samoan Gangstas (a 3D on Anoai) on Blood, Sweat and Beers and over the Briscoe Boys in their last defence before Heatwave, all with their relatives' help, and the Hardcore Innovators then cane the second generation, DDT the two of them and walk off with the belts; at Heatwave Cactus Jack and Tommy Dreamer put D-Von through a table with a Double DDT and win the titles. In September they lose a tag title match to the Whole F**kin' Show on Revolution when simultaneous finishers beat Bubba Ray and D-Von, D-Von is pinned by Shawn Michaels's Super Kick despite interference from Big Dick Jr. and Ultimo Dudley II, Bubba Ray pins Michaels with a 3D in a non-title match, and the mystery Dudley, Slyk Tayshaun, attacks them both. At Anarchy Rulz in September 2007 the second generation of Dudleyz break up the Champions versus Champions match, Bubba Ray and D-Von put the Hardcore Innovators down with a 3D, and the Dudleyz take both sets of tag belts from ringside; D-Von beats Tommy Dreamer on Blood, Sweat and Beers, and on the first Revolution of October Shawn Michaels pins Bubba Ray with a Super Kick. Paul Heyman books the Three Way Dance for the tag titles at Guilty As Charged, and there the Dudley Boyz pin Rob Van Dam after Michaels's Super Kick takes him down and win the unified belts, which the Hardcore Innovators carry out of the arena. In November 2007 Bubba Ray and D-Von, standing with the Dudley Family, challenge the Hardcore Innovators, who walk around with all four tag belts, to a title match at November To Remember XV; Slyk Tayshaun Dudley then chairs the Dudley Family and the two of them, and D-Von tells him that he is fouling his own doorstep. On Blood, Sweat and Beers Paul Heyman announces the Undisputed ECW Tag Team belts and a match in which the Dudley Boyz and the Innovators unify the titles, and the diary's preview of the card bills it with the Dudley Boyz as the champions. At November To Remember XV (30 November 2007 in the diary's history) Bubba Ray and D-Von, with Big Dick Jr., Ultimo Dudley II and Daizy, beat the Hardcore Innovators in a weapons match: D-Von lifts Beulah McGillicutty for Bubba's Superbomb through a table, and a Dudley Death Drop through a flaming table pins Tommy Dreamer; they raise the Undisputed ECW Tag Team Titles, and Slyk Tayshaun Dudley then comes to the ring with a baseball bat and beats down every one of his relatives. On Revolution on the first Monday of December they defend the Undisputed belts against the Thomaselli brothers, the match is restarted as a Three Way Dance with Slyk and Dick Jr., and Slyk breaks up Bubba's pin on Brandon and makes Bubba tap to the Boston Crabs. The diary's next preview bills them as the 'Original Dudleyz'; on Saturday, with Ultimo Dudley II, they chair and powerbomb the Thomasellis through a table after the new champions' first defence.

name: The Iron Saints

tenures.source: The diary's own posts bill the group; its first mention is at /promotions/ecw-worldwide-nevermore/archive/month-2006-08-p111-166.html.

caption: A stable of preaching youngsters who arrive on F' The Mainstream in August 2006 vowing to rid ECW of sinners, call out one wrestler a week for punishment, and win the First Blood Match against The Acolytes at Heatwave. In February 2007 the Iron Saints, Salvatore and Brandon Thomaselli, beat the Dudley Boys, the Blue World Order and the FBI in a row, jump the Whole F**kin' Show on Blood, Sweat and Beers and throw Traci through a table, and take the Undisputed ECW World Tag Team Championships at Living Dangerously with a Spike Powerbomb on Shawn Michaels after Rob Van Dam steps off the apron; they lose the belts at Baptism Of Fire in the first Halflife Handicap match and in April beat Paul London and Brian Kendrick. In April 2007 the Iron Saints beat the Full Blooded Italians, lose to the Canadian Connection and then to Monsters Inc with the Nest's interference, after which Raven orders Vito to hit one of his own brothers with a Vito Driver. In May they object to Vito bringing their sister Kelly into ECW, side with Paul Burchill against the Nest (Salvatore is the masked man on Blood, Sweat and Beers), beat Vito and CM Punk, beat the Nest in a six-man tag with Burchill and lose to Vito and Punk on Revolution; at Hardcore Heaven they beat Monsters Inc with steel chairs, then are chokeslammed and taken away on gurneys after Vito turns on them. On Revolution in June 2007 Brandon and Salvatore return from hospital with chairs and wreck the Nest as Paul Burchill is about to be powerbombed through tables; at Wrestlepalooza Vito turns on CM Punk and, with his brothers, beats him in the tag match Heyman gave them. In July Raven makes them wrestle each other (Brandon wins with a T-Bone Suplex and Salvatore hugs him), Mark Calaway beats Brandon with a Chokeslam in the tag match against Vito and Calaway, and at Summer Assylum the Saints beat CM Punk and Monsters Inc. In August Brandon beats Afa and Salvatore saves him from the Samoan Gangstas. In August 2007 Brandon is beaten by Nate Hatred when James Mitchell's cane intervenes, and both brothers are at ringside with Vito when Raven's Nest turn on him. In September Sal beats Chris Jericho with a Tiger Driver, Brandon is beaten by Rhino and by Paul Burchill, Sal is beaten by Burchill, and the brothers come to Burchill's aid with Vito and Kelly. In October 2007 Sal beats Jerry Lynn with a Senton Bomb, and the brothers announce 'Thomaselli Thomaselli '08', the Green Party's candidacy for president; Brandon wins the 'Presidential Primary' Match against Yoshihiro Tajiri with a T-Bone suplex, and Sal loses to Kurt Angle's Ankle Lock. In November 2007 Brandon beats Scorpio Sky with a Crossface Chickenwing and Sal beats Teddy Hart with a Senton Bomb on the first F' The Mainstream recap; the brothers lose to the Hardcore Innovators (a Double DDT on Brandon) on Blood, Sweat and Beers, Sal loses to Shawn Michaels's Sweet Chin Music, to Chris Hero, who then chokes him out, and to Andrew Martin in a parody gimmick, and Brandon loses to Nate Hatred's Decapitator Lariat and to Martin in a second parody. At November To Remember XV Vito beats CM Punk clean with a Vito Driver and walks to the ring in Paul Burchill's entourage with his sister Kelly, Steven Regal and Shane Douglas. Sal and Brandon wrestle as Thomaselli-Thomaselli '08: on Revolution on the first Monday of December they lose the Three Way Dance for the Undisputed ECW Tag Team Titles; the F' The Mainstream recap has Jushin Lyger and Rey Mysterio Jr. beat them in 9:22, and on the Saturday show Slyk and Dick Dudley beat them with a Boston Crabs on Brandon before the Original Dudleyz chair Brandon and powerbomb Sal through a table. Vito and Burchill beat CM Punk and Goliath by disqualification on Revolution, and on the Saturday show Rhino beats Vito in a number one contendership match.

name: The Blue World Order

tenures.source: The diary's own posts bill the group; its first mention is at /promotions/ecw-worldwide-nevermore/archive/month-2006-09-p177-194.html.

caption: A comic stable that returns to Revolution in September 2006 and sets about pranking Charlie Pag, Paul Burchill and Raven before Big Stevie Cool and Hollywood Nova win the tag belts. In February 2007 Big Stevie Cool beats The Great Sasuke at Living Dangerously with a Stevie Kick that catches him in mid-air; in March the Sasuke World Order drag Big Stevie Cool, Hollywood Nova and Da Blue Guy under the ring, and at Baptism Of Fire Big Stevie Cool and Hollywood Nova turn on Da Blue Guy and kneel with the cult to worship The Great Sasuke. In June 2007 Al Snow and Big Stevie Cool pair up against Rhino, Stevie superkicking Rhino through a table at Wrestlepalooza and Snow thanking him for it afterwards with the mannequin head; on Revolution in July Snow is named a new member, 'BW Snow', and Head 'Head of Bluecurity'. The bWo spray-paint Rhino, are beaten 4-on-1 on Revolution, Stevie Kicks the sWo and sprays 'bWo' on every one of them, lose to the Dudley Boyz in the first defence of the Dudleyville Hardcore Titles when the sWo's Chessman and Oz hit them with the belts, and prank Oz by hanging the sWo's sign on the ladies' locker room. In August 2007 the bWo take BW Snow to the ring ('WE WANT HEAD'), are floored by Espiritu and Escoria, and beat the sWo with a Stevie Kick on Oz on Revolution; at Heatwave Big Stevie Cool loses to Big Sasuke Cool when six Sasukes emerge from under the ring. In September the bWo beat the sWo when Hollywood Nova, disguised as Chessman, turns on them, beat Oz on Blood, Sweat and Beers and beat the Second Generation of Dudleyz on F' The Mainstream; Big Stevie Cool and Big Sasuke Cool meet again at Anarchy Rulz. At Anarchy Rulz in September 2007 Big Stevie Cool loses to Big Sasuke Cool; in October the bWo beat the sWo on Revolution with a Stevie Kick on Chessman, free BW Snow with Big Stevie Cool in a Sasuke mask, and lose the next match when the 'mole' (who proves to be Big Stevie Cool) attacks them from under the ring. At Guilty As Charged Big Stevie Cool turns on Hollywood Nova and BW Snow with Stevie Kicks and leaves with Sasuke; the diary's Bam Bam Exam reports ECW releasing the Blue Meanie.

name: The Cult of Sasuke

tenures.source: The diary's own posts bill the group; its first mention is at /promotions/ecw-worldwide-nevermore/archive/month-2006-09-p195-231.html.

caption: A masked Super Juniors cult led by The Great Sasuke, who arrives on F' The Mainstream in September 2006 with five disciples vowing mayhem, strips the Iron Saints and the Dudley Boys to their underwear, stages ritual assaults on LA Park and Jushin Lyger, and wins LA Park for the group at Anarchy Rulz. In December 2006 The Great Sasuke renames the group the Sasuke World Order and announces that it will take over F' The Mainstream and then the world. In February 2007 the group, now the Sasuke World Order, tear off their shirts to show sWo logos spray-painted on their chests and The Great Sasuke loses to Big Stevie Cool at Living Dangerously; in March the cult drag Big Stevie Cool, Hollywood Nova and Da Blue Guy under the ring, and at Baptism Of Fire Stevie and Nova, now under Sasuke's spell, turn on Da Blue Guy and kneel to worship him. In April the Dudley Boys, as the self-styled enforcers of ECW, take on the cult, and Sasuke hangs life-size mannequins of the Dudleys from the rafters. In June 2007 the Sasuke World Order storm the ring on Revolution to claim a place as a twelfth World Cup team; in the pool stage they lose to Team USA twice, lose once to Italy when Oz's chair swing backfires and win once by swapping masks, and, with Cuervo's spray paint costing Italy its last match against Team USA, qualify by a single bonus point; they beat Samoa in the quarter-final with Oz's distraction, Cuervo's 2x4 and Sasuke's wits. They lose the semi-final to Japan when Tajiri, in Sasuke's mask, pins Chessman; after the tournament Sasuke beats Tajiri with Oz's lead pipe and the sWo paint the ECW flag, until two Chessmen and Big Stevie Cool's bWo invade and spray 'bWo' on the sWo, and in August Oz, tricked by the bWo into the ladies' locker room, is Super Kicked by Shawn Michaels. In August 2007 the sWo take on Espiritu and Escoria, who argue over 'We're overtaking' and 'We're taking over', brawl with the bWo on Revolution and lose to them before Heatwave, where Big Sasuke Cool beats Big Stevie Cool by hiding five extra Sasukes under the ring and a Michinoku Driver. In September Hollywood Nova, painted as Chessman, tricks the sWo, Sasuke pins Nova with a school boy, Oz is pinned by a Stevie Kick, Sasuke loses the International All Action Title Match to CM Punk when Monsters Inc. interfere, and Chris Hero pins Sasuke on F' The Mainstream. At Anarchy Rulz in September 2007 Big Sasuke Cool beats Big Stevie Cool with a Michinoku Driver after a low blow, as Chessman and four men dressed as Hollywood Nova run in. In October the sWo take BW Snow hostage and show him a Kevin Nash and John Cena match, are tricked when the bWo send Big Stevie Cool in as a masked 'Sasuke' to free him and show the real Sasuke 'The Best of Monday Night Raw', and lose on Blood, Sweat and Beers when a masked 'mole' attacks the bWo's men from under the ring. At Guilty As Charged, with the loser to disband, Big Sasuke Cool pins Hollywood Nova, Superkicks Chessman and leaves with Big Stevie Cool as the True World Order; the diary's Bam Bam Exam then lists Chessman, Cuervo, Escoria, Espiritu and Oz among the workers ECW is releasing.

name: The F.B.I.

tenures.source: The diary's own posts bill the group; its first mention is at /promotions/ecw-worldwide-nevermore/archive/month-2006-09-p195-231.html.

caption: Little Guido's Full Blooded Italians, hired by Charlie Pag, Raven and Paul Burchill in September 2006 to destroy the Blue World Order for a tag title shot, who lose to the bWo on Revolution and beat Shawn Michaels down five on one in September. In April 2007 the Full Blooded Italians lose to the Iron Saints (a Spike Powerbomb on Tony Mamaluke); in May Shawn Michaels pins Tony Mamaluke without tagging Rob Van Dam, and in June the Hardcore Innovators beat them with a Double DDT on Mamaluke. In the World Cup of July 2007 Little Guido, Tony Mamaluke and Big Sal E Graziano play for Team Italy; Guido's Sicilian Crab beats Brian Kendrick, but the sWo's tricks and Team USA's wins knock them out in Pool A.

name: Los Increibles

tenures.source: The diary's own posts bill the group; its first mention is at /promotions/ecw-worldwide-nevermore/archive/month-2006-10-p244-324.html.

caption: Rey Mysterio Jr. and Juventud Guerrera, who end their best-of-seven series at Anarchy Rulz with a hug and team up as Los Increibles on the first Revolution of October 2006, beating Michael Shane and Frankie Kazarian with a Double Springboard Legdrop, and win again with a Double Toprope Guillotina the week after. As part of Team Mexico they lose the Lucha Libre six-man tag at Living Dangerously; after the Ultimate Jeopardy match at Baptism Of Fire they turn on Eddie Guerrero with a Hurricanrana, and in April they beat Los Guerreros on Revolution with the Juvi Driver on Eddie and lose the rematch on Blood, Sweat and Beers. In April 2007 Los Increibles beat Los Guerreros on Blood, Sweat and Beers (Rey Mysterio Jr.'s Tornado DDT on Chavo) to earn a tag title match at Cyberslam, where the Whole F**kin' Show keep the belts in the Ladder Match. In May AJ Styles pins Juventud Guerrera on his debut, and in June Juvi beats AJ in a non-title match after AJ kisses Francine, while Rey Mysterio Jr. loses to AJ's low blow and small package. In June 2007 Rey Mysterio Jr. prepares for the World Cup with Team Mexico while Juventud Guerrera, who is not in the tournament, loses to AJ Styles with the low blow and the foot-on-the-rope finishes; in August Juvi beats Rey in the first match of their revived series with a 450 Splash. At Guilty As Charged in October 2007 Rey Mysterio Jr., saying that Juventud Guerrera 'was dead weight' and the reason they never won the tag titles, joins the four-way Stairway To Hell Match for the World Television Championship, and Guerrera, returning through the crowd with a chair, hits all four men; the next night he beats Mysterio with a 450 Splash. In November 2007 Rey Mysterio Jr. and Juventud Guerrera, who 'cannot stand one another', are booked together against Ultimo Dragon and Christopher Daniels on Blood, Sweat and Beers, and the alliance breaks down when Mysterio floors his own partner with a punch; Guerrera pins Daniels with a 450 Splash.

name: Monsters Inc.

tenures.source: The diary's own posts bill the group; its first mention is at /promotions/ecw-worldwide-nevermore/archive/month-2006-11-p339-360.html.

caption: Abyss and Goliath, who take the tag belts from the Blue World Order at Guilty As Charged with a Double Chokeslam and keep them on Revolution against the Dudley Boys with the Iron Saints' help. In February and March 2007 Abyss and Goliath stay with Raven, who demands a tag title shot for his 'monsters' and is refused by Shane Douglas; at Baptism Of Fire Goliath is the first man eliminated from the Baptism Of Fire match, pushed into the flames by eight others, and Abyss is thrown over by Sabu and Tommy Dreamer. In April 2007 Monsters Inc help CM Punk beat Lance Storm and beat the Iron Saints on Revolution; in May they hold Kelly Thomaselli for Raven and, at Hardcore Heaven, are beaten by the Iron Saints, an upset, before chokeslamming them in a second attack with Vito. In June they beat Team England's Nigel McGuinness with a Double Chokeslam and lose to Paul Burchill and Davey Boy Smith. At Wrestlepalooza in June 2007 Goliath is found laid out in the car park and Abyss loses to Paul Burchill's Release German Suplex through tables; in July they lose to Mark Calaway (a Chokeslam on Abyss) and, in the handicap match Raven books against Vito, Vito wins with Calaway's help, and at Summer Assylum they lose to the Iron Saints in the six-man tag with CM Punk; in August Vito beats Goliath with a Shining Wizard. On Blood, Sweat and Beers in August 2007 Vito Thomaselli beats them with Shane Douglas's help; at Heatwave Goliath carries a key to the cage door of the Barbed Wire Cage Match so that they can enter, and Vito drives them out with a Double DDT; in September they stand by Raven and CM Punk, hitting Vito and Burchill with Double Chokeslams. At Anarchy Rulz in September 2007 Abyss's Big Boot hits CM Punk by mistake and Vito Thomaselli's springboard somersault plancha takes both monsters down; in October they stand by Punk, and at Guilty As Charged they hold Vito for Punk's chair shots in the Last Man Standing Match (a Black Hole Slam by Abyss, a Chokeslam by Goliath) until the referee stops it. In November 2007 Abyss and Goliath interfere for Raven's Nest in the main events on Revolution, where Shane Douglas fights them off with a chair and Chris Jericho clears them with another; Abyss taps to Jericho's Liontamer in the six-man tag on Blood, Sweat and Beers. At November To Remember XV Abyss and Goliath escort the champion Raven to the ring and stand in front of his corner for the Loser Leaves ECW Match. On the Saturday show they beat down Paul Burchill with Raven's Nest until Sabu and The Sandman, in 'ECW Enforcer' shirts, clear Abyss and Goliath; on Revolution on the first Monday of December Abyss flattens Vito Thomaselli with a Black Hole Slam and Sabu chairs him out of the ring.

name: The New Age Enterprise

tenures.source: The diary's own posts bill the group; its first mention is at /promotions/ecw-worldwide-nevermore/archive/month-2006-11-p339-360.html.

caption: The faction around Charlie Pag, Raven and Paul Burchill that bans the Blue World Order from ringside in October 2006, arranges Pag's wedding to Stephanie Mcintosh, and takes the World Heavyweight and World Tag Team Championships at Guilty As Charged before the bWo and Paul Heyman's return end its rule on Revolution in November. Its hold is broken in November 2006, and it returns on the last Blood, Sweat and Beers of the year, when Raven and Paul Burchill turn on Owen Hart and Rhino and Charlie Pag, Stephanie Mcintosh, Abyss and Goliath walk out to join them; in January 2007 Vito joins after beating Rhino, and in February CM Punk joins and Abyss, blamed for losing the tag titles, is beaten down and cast out. In February 2007 Raven and Charlie Pag fall out over who calls the shots and patch it up, and at Living Dangerously the group take the International All Action and World Television Championships (CM Punk beats Christopher Daniels with Raven's chair, Paul Burchill pins Bret Hart with the C-4) before Raven beats Sabu for the World Heavyweight Championship the next night, throws Charlie Pag and Stephanie Mcintosh through the ringside tables and re-forms the stable as Raven's Nest.

name: The Whole F**kin' Show

tenures.source: The diary's own posts bill the group; its first mention is at /promotions/ecw-worldwide-nevermore/archive/month-2006-11-p386-412.html.

caption: Rob Van Dam and Shawn Michaels, the Show Stealer and the Showstopper, who team on Revolution in November 2006, beat the Acolytes, take the Undisputed ECW World Tag Team Championships from Monsters Inc. at November To Remember with the 420 Splash, make Traci their manager and keep the belts through January and February 2007 while the two partners fall out over her. The partners fall out at Living Dangerously when Rob Van Dam steps off the apron and lets the Iron Saints pin Shawn Michaels for the belts, make up the next night on Blood, Sweat and Beers when Michaels explains himself, trap the Iron Saints with Traci's help, and win the belts back at Baptism Of Fire in the first Halflife Handicap match with a Five Star Frog Splash on Salvatore; in April Rob Van Dam and Traci kiss, and Rob Van Dam is booked against Chris Jericho for the Television Championship at Cyberslam. At Cyberslam in April 2007 Rob Van Dam beats Chris Jericho for the Television Championship in the Lumberjack Match and the team keep the tag belts in the Ladder Match against Los Increibles. In May AJ Styles's debut and Rob Van Dam's jealousy over Traci split the partners, and at Hardcore Heaven Shawn Michaels, bloodied and alone, keeps the tag belts over the Canadian Connection with a third Sweet Chin Music on Christian while Van Dam is away helping Traci; Van Dam then loses the Television Championship to AJ Styles, helped by the Canadian Connection's hockey sticks. In June Van Dam and Michaels refuse to tag each other and Michaels slaps Van Dam, then Traci locks them in a locker room and they make up. In June 2007 Van Dam and Michaels make peace with the Hardcore Innovators, trading hugs and signs on each other's backs, and at Wrestlepalooza keep the World Tag Team Championship over them when Michaels's Diving Elbow and Van Dam's Five Star Frog Splash win simultaneous covers, before the Dudley Boys, back in ECW, attack them. At Summer Assylum they win the Tables Match against the Dudleys with Michaels's Sweet Chin Music through a table on D-Von, are DDT'd by the Innovators afterwards, beat the Innovators on Blood, Sweat and Beers when Ultimo Dudley II hits Cactus Jack with a lid, and in August Traci is pranked by the bWo. At Heatwave in August 2007 they run out after the Innovators win the Dudleyville Hardcore Titles and attack Cactus Jack and Tommy Dreamer with a Superkick, an Enziguiri, a Flying Elbow Drop and a Five Star Frog Splash, telling them there is room for only one World Tag Team Champions; the Dudley Family and the Innovators then brawl with them in a no contest on Blood, Sweat and Beers. In September they keep the belts over the Dudley Boyz on Revolution with simultaneous finishers, Shawn Michaels pins D-Von with a Super Kick the week after, and they accept the Innovators' challenge for a Champions versus Champions match at Anarchy Rulz. When Michaels walks in on Traci changing and covers her as footsteps approach, Rob Van Dam takes the wrong meaning and the partners fall out for two weeks, Van Dam leaving Michaels alone against the Dudleyz in a non-title match, until they hug it out backstage on the last Monday before the pay-per-view. At Anarchy Rulz in September 2007 they lose the Champions versus Champions match by a no contest after the Dudley Family run in. In October Traci is carried out on a stretcher after the Dudleyz drop her onto the guard rail while Michaels and Van Dam are distracted, and the partners quarrel over which stipulation to ask for until Paul Heyman books a match with ladders, chairs, canes and flaming tables; at Guilty As Charged Michaels shoves D-Von through a burning table, then his Super Kick catches Van Dam in mid-air and Bubba Ray pins Van Dam, ending the reign. On Blood, Sweat and Beers Van Dam punches Michaels and later calls for a reunion, and Michaels hugs him and Super Kicks him again ('that Super Kick last night was no accident and nor was this'). In November 2007 Shawn Michaels apologises on Revolution for the Super Kick at Guilty As Charged and calls Rob Van Dam his brother; Van Dam asks for a one-on-one match and, when Michaels says that he cannot fight his brother, hits him with the Van Daminator and a chair, and on Blood, Sweat and Beers he appears at the entrance to distract Michaels in his match with CM Punk. Michaels refuses the match again, but the two save each other from the True World Order and beat it together on Revolution, and Paul Heyman, 'sorry to go over your head', books Rob Van Dam against Shawn Michaels at November To Remember XV; on the last Blood, Sweat and Beers before it they are on opposite sides of a tag match and still join to beat down Kurt Angle, and on the last Revolution they jump off opposite corners together onto the brawl that wrecks the ring. At November To Remember XV Shawn Michaels and Rob Van Dam walk to the ring together to Pantera and trade a contest of alphabet moves (RVD: 'It's November 2007, bro... they're on strike') before the match the diary rates A: Michaels beats Van Dam with a Sweet Chin Music that drives into his face the chair Van Dam is carrying, and both bow to the crowd. On Revolution on the first Monday of December Van Dam hugs Michaels backstage and says he wants a rematch, 'since we're both in Masters of Pain Qualifiers'; on the Saturday show Van Dam beats The Great Sasuke by knockout after the Van Daminator, Stevie Richards runs in and Michaels clears him with Sweet Chin Music.

name: The Canadian Connection

tenures.source: The diary's own posts bill the group; its first mention is at /promotions/ecw-worldwide-nevermore/archive/month-2006-12-p434-506.html.

caption: Chris Jericho, Christian and Chris Benoit, who join forces at November To Remember after Benoit and Eddie Guerrero fight to a draw, take the name on Revolution in December 2006 and preach the superiority of Canada, and feud with Eddie Guerrero, Rey Mysterio Jr. and Juventud Guerrera (Team Mexico), against whom they win the six-man tag at Got Blood?. In February 2007 the group beat Team Mexico in the Lucha Libre six-man tag at Living Dangerously with Christian's Unprettier on Juventud Guerrera, and win the three-way Ultimate Jeopardy match at Baptism Of Fire against Team Mexico and Team JAPAN, when Chris Benoit, the last man in, eliminates Jushin Lyger, Ultimo Dragon, Eddie Guerrero and Juventud Guerrera with the Crossface and a Diving Headbutt; Christian attacks the Whole F**kin' Show with brass knuckles after the pay-per-view, and in April the group beat Paul London and Brian Kendrick and take the ECW World Television Championship when Chris Jericho pins Bret Hart in the Triangle Match. In April 2007 the Canadian Connection beat the Iron Saints, take Raven's deal to jump the masked man and, at Cyberslam, win the three-way dance for the number one contendership to the World Tag Team Championship over Los Guerreros and the Dudley Boys, while Chris Jericho loses the Television Championship to Rob Van Dam. In May they beat Lyger and Ultimo Dragon, ally with AJ Styles and Chris Hero, lose the tag title match at Hardcore Heaven when Shawn Michaels pins Christian, and help AJ Styles take the Television Championship with hockey sticks; in June Don Callis coaches Team Canada, with Lance Storm, Chris Benoit, Christian, Chris Jericho, Teddy Hart and Bobby Roode. In July 2007 Jericho, Christian and Benoit play for Team Canada in the World Cup. By the end of that month the diary reports that Christian has signed with the WWA and left ECW; in August Jericho forces Benoit to tap to the Walls Of Jericho on Revolution, and Owen Hart, whom Jericho mocks as an old-timer, challenges him to a match at Heatwave.

name: Raven's Nest

tenures.source: The diary's own posts bill the group; its first mention is at /promotions/ecw-worldwide-nevermore/archive/month-2007-02-p638-649.html.

caption: Raven's own stable, announced as the 'newly re-formed Raven's Nest' on the last Blood, Sweat and Beers of February 2007, when Raven beats Sabu for the World Heavyweight Championship with Paul Burchill and Goliath's help, throws Charlie Pag and Stephanie Mcintosh through the ringside tables ('time to take out the trash') and is joined by Abyss, Vito and CM Punk. In March Raven demands a tag title shot for his 'monsters' and is refused by Shane Douglas, beats Douglas at Baptism Of Fire with Punk's help to become the Revolution commissioner, and sees Paul Burchill win the Baptism Of Fire match for the Nest. In April 2007 Raven, as commissioner, fires Owen Hart, and the Nest, with the Canadian Connection's help, unmask the masked man who has been attacking them, who turns out to be Vito, while a voice on the PA says it will not be that easy; at Cyberslam Raven keeps the World Heavyweight Championship over Rhino in the Steel Cage Match with Paul Burchill as special referee, and Burchill then turns on Raven with a C-4 and leaves the Nest: on the next Blood, Sweat and Beers Burchill and Shane Douglas, the real masked man, tell how the plan ran for seven months. In May the Nest (Raven, CM Punk, Abyss, Goliath and Vito) take Kelly Thomaselli, Vito's sister, as a hostage against Burchill, and at Hardcore Heaven Raven beats Burchill when Punk threatens to throw Kelly off the stage and then does; in June the Nest face Burchill, Shane Douglas, Team England and Davey Boy Smith. In June 2007 Raven has Paul Heyman clear the arena so that the Nest can face Paul Burchill alone and beats him down with a run of finishers, then collapses when a chanting video plays; on Revolution he admits he commissioned the videos and hijacked ecw.com himself, until the Iron Saints, out of hospital, wreck the Nest with chairs. At Wrestlepalooza Vito turns on CM Punk and the Saints leave Punk and Abyss on the girders under the stage, Burchill beats Abyss, and Raven keeps the World Heavyweight Championship over both Harts and is Chokeslammed by the mystery signing, Mark Calaway. In July Calaway and Vito beat Raven and Punk and Monsters Inc, Raven turns Vito's First Blood Match into a pinfall match, shocks Calaway and Vito with cattle prods and sends the Nest after Calaway and the Saints, a Heyman eight-man tag ends in a no contest, and at Summer Assylum the Iron Saints beat Punk and Monsters Inc, Vito powerbombing Punk through a table, before Raven keeps his title over Calaway when Rhino Gores Calaway. In August Goliath loses to Vito and Raven tells him he cannot face Vito at Heatwave. In August 2007 the Nest run in on the mass brawl and on Paul Burchill and Shane Douglas; at Heatwave Raven's cage stipulation, Monsters Inc.'s key and CM Punk's GTS on Vito Thomaselli after Burchill's top-of-the-cage Corkscrew Cross Body let Raven keep the World Heavyweight Championship, and on Blood, Sweat and Beers he reads out clause 17.2a of the contract, which voids a title change after outside interference, and uses clause 24.17e, as Commissioner, to hold Burchill's and Douglas's contracts over them. In September Raven brings in Alexis Laree, 'the cream of the CZW crop', Punk keeps the International All Action Championship, Raven hits Burchill with the Raven Effect after his wins, and Raven is booked to defend against Rhino at Anarchy Rulz. At Anarchy Rulz in September 2007 Nate Hatred beats Paul Burchill and Burchill is fired, Raven pins Rhino after Mark Calaway's Chokeslam and is then chokeslammed by Calaway. In October Owen Hart makes Raven tap on Revolution, Raven loses a cage match to Chris Jericho and is chokeslammed by Calaway; at Guilty As Charged Raven, as Commissioner, books his own match, pins Jericho with a Raven Effect and becomes seven-time champion, and on Blood, Sweat and Beers the company's owner returns, strips him of his powers as Commissioner, gives booking power back to Paul Heyman and books Paul Burchill against him for November To Remember XV. Alexis Laree wins the first Lioness Championship, and Nattie Neidhart joins the Nest as 'the anonymous blonde'. In November 2007 Paul Heyman, back in power, tells Raven on Revolution that nobody in the arena is comfortable seeing him as their champion, has CM Punk stripped of the International All Action Championship by security guards, and says that Paul Burchill will beat Raven at November To Remember; the whole Nest assaults Burchill on the second Revolution until Chris Jericho's chair shots and a C-4 turn it, and Raven is left alone in the ring. Alexis Laree and Nathalie work together against Jazz and Kelly Thomaselli, and on the third Blood, Sweat and Beers Heyman makes Raven's match a Loser Leaves ECW Match. At November To Remember XV Raven loses the Loser Leaves ECW Match to Paul Burchill and is out of ECW; CM Punk, Alexis Laree and the others lose their leader. On the Saturday show Punk tells Burchill, Vito Thomaselli and Shane Douglas that Raven 'ensured that I was ready to take his place as the leader of the Nest' and loses to Burchill with a C-4; the Nest's run-in is cleared by the ECW Enforcers. Punk and Goliath lose on Revolution on the first Monday of December to Burchill and Vito Thomaselli by disqualification, when Punk low-blows Vito.

name: Crouching Lyger, Hidden Dragon

tenures.source: The diary's own posts bill the group; its first mention is at /promotions/ecw-worldwide-nevermore/archive/month-2007-03-p650-705.html.

caption: Jushin Lyger and Ultimo Dragon, who make their tag team debut on Revolution in March 2007 by beating Michael Shane and Frankie Kazarian with a Corkscrew Moonsault over Lyger's back, beat the Briscoe Boys and the Hardy Boys, lose to the Canadian Connection, the Iron Saints (with the Canadian Connection's interference) and the Whole F**kin' Show, and join Hayabusa as Team JAPAN in the Ultimate Jeopardy match at Baptism Of Fire. In April 2007 Lyger pins Brian Kendrick with a 450 Splash and Ultimo Dragon pins Michael Shane with a Moonsault from Lyger's shoulders; in May they lose to the Iron Saints and to the Canadian Connection (Walls Of Jericho on Lyger), and then beat Chavo Guerrero Jr. with a 450 Splash; in June they lose to Shawn Michaels when Rob Van Dam runs in to save him with a Five Star Frog Splash on Ultimo Dragon. Lyger, captain of Team Japan, and Ultimo Dragon play in the World Cup of July 2007 and are beaten in the final by Paul Burchill; in August Ultimo Dragon runs in to save Juventud Guerrera and Francine from AJ Styles and Christopher Daniels and is booked against Styles for the Television Championship.

name: Team JAPAN

tenures.source: The diary's own posts bill the group; its first mention is at /promotions/ecw-worldwide-nevermore/archive/month-2007-03-p650-705.html.

caption: Jushin Lyger, Ultimo Dragon and Hayabusa, who come together in March 2007 when Hayabusa returns from injury to flip over the Canadian Connection and Team Mexico after a brawl, and are added by Paul Heyman to the Ultimate Jeopardy match at Baptism Of Fire; Hayabusa, Lyger and Ultimo Dragon are eliminated in turn, and the Canadian Connection win the match. The full Japanese squad for the Wrestling World Cup of July 2007 is Jushin Lyger (captain), Ultimo Dragon, Hayabusa, Kensuke Sasaki, Masato Tanaka and Yoshihiro Tajiri. They beat Scotland twice and split with Canada, finish level on points with them, and win the draw to top Pool C; they beat Ireland in the quarter-final and the sWo in the semi-final (Tajiri, in Sasuke's mask, pins Chessman), and lose the final to England when Paul Burchill, last of his team, beats Tanaka, Lyger and Ultimo Dragon.

name: Team Mexico

tenures.source: The diary's own posts bill the group; its first mention is at /promotions/ecw-worldwide-nevermore/archive/ppv-got-blood-p539-555.html.

caption: Eddie Guerrero, Rey Mysterio Jr. and Juventud Guerrera, the trio the Canadian Connection challenge to a six-man tag at Got Blood?; in February 2007 they lose the Lucha Libre six-man tag at Living Dangerously when Christian hits Juventud Guerrera with the Unprettier while the referee checks the others, accept the Canadian Connection's challenge to an Extreme Cage War at Baptism Of Fire, and lose the three-way Ultimate Jeopardy match there; Eddie blames Juvi, and Rey and Juvi leave him on the mat, which ends the team. The full Mexican squad for the Wrestling World Cup of July 2007 is Eddie Guerrero (captain), Chavo Guerrero Jr., Rey Mysterio Jr., Psicosis and Ricky Marvin. They win all four Pool B matches and top the pool, beat Canada in the quarter-final (Mysterio's Super Hurricanrana on Lance Storm, Guerrero's Texas Cloverleaf on Chris Benoit and Frog Splash on Chris Jericho) and lose the semi-final to England when Paul Burchill eliminates Mysterio and Guerrero with a Double C-4.

name: Los Guerreros

tenures.source: The diary's own posts bill the group; its first mention is at /promotions/ecw-worldwide-nevermore/archive/month-2007-04-p753-787.html.

caption: Eddie Guerrero and Chavo Guerrero Jr., who re-form the team on Blood, Sweat and Beers in April 2007 when Chavo makes his debut with a Superkick on Juventud Guerrera in the middle of Eddie's brawl with Juvi; they lose to Los Increibles on Revolution and beat them on the next Blood, Sweat and Beers, when Chavo covers Rey Mysterio after Eddie's Frog Splash. In April 2007 Los Guerreros beat Paul London and Brian Kendrick (Eddie's Frog Splash on London), lose to Los Increibles, and at Cyberslam are the first team eliminated in the three-way dance for the tag title number one contendership, by the Dudley Boys with 3Ds and a Spike Powerbomb through tables. In the World Cup of July 2007 Eddie and Chavo Guerrero Jr. lead Team Mexico, and the diary's previews for August name Los Guerreros as the third challengers for the Dudley Boyz's Dudleyville Hardcore Titles. On Revolution in August 2007 Los Guerreros challenge the Dudley Boyz for the Dudleyville Hardcore Titles and lose to a 3D on Chavo, the second generation of Dudleyz playing a large part in the result.

name: The Hart Foundation

tenures.source: The diary's own posts bill the group; its first mention is at /promotions/ecw-worldwide-nevermore/archive/ppv-living-dangerously-p620-637.html.

caption: Bret Hart and Owen Hart, the brothers who feud with the New Age Enterprise and Raven's Nest through February, March and April 2007: they guard each other against the Enterprise's numbers, with Owen banned from ringside for Bret's matches, and Owen is eliminated by Rhino near the end of the Baptism Of Fire match after Bret has been replaced in it by Paul Burchill. In April 2007 Raven fires Owen Hart as commissioner; Owen beats Kensuke Sasaki with a Sharpshooter in the semi-final of the Number One Contendership Tournament and loses the final to Rhino when the masked man's chair misses Raven and hits him, while Bret beats Goliath at Cyberslam for a title shot. In May the brothers fall out: after beating Paul London and Brian Kendrick with matching Sharpshooters Bret pulls Owen off a cover, and Paul Heyman makes their Hardcore Heaven match the number one contendership, which Owen wins with a Diving Headbutt; in June Heyman books Owen against Raven at Wrestlepalooza and Bret in a Triangle Match for the title. In June 2007 the brothers argue on Revolution over who will take the World Heavyweight Championship, Bret calling Owen's Hardcore Heaven win a fluke, and Bret beats Doug Williams with the Sharpshooter; at Wrestlepalooza they take turns with the Sharpshooter and the Ankle Lock in the Triangle Match with Raven, Owen makes Bret tap, and Raven then pins Owen with a Raven Effect onto a chair and keeps the belt. Bret does not appear again in this run; Owen beats Lance Storm with the Sharpshooter on Blood, Sweat and Beers after Summer Assylum, is mocked there by Chris Jericho, challenges Jericho for Heatwave, and in August beats Chris Hero with a Sharpshooter in the tag match with Jerry Lynn.

name: The Hardcore Innovators

tenures.source: The diary's own posts bill the group; its first mention is at /promotions/ecw-worldwide-nevermore/archive/month-2007-06-p967-1005.html.

caption: Cactus Jack and Tommy Dreamer, who team in April 2007 after Cactus, weeping backstage, saves Dreamer from Chris Benoit with a barbed-wire 2x4, and in May win the Hardcore Heaven match against Chris Benoit and The Sandman for the number one contendership to the World Tag Team Championship, when Cactus's Double Arm DDT pins Benoit as Dreamer drives The Sandman through a DDT on the concrete. Billed as 'The Hardcore Innovators' on Revolution in June 2007, they bring Singapore canes to the ring and win in turn over the Full Blooded Italians, over a second team on Blood, Sweat and Beers and on the next Revolution, and over Mark Briscoe, each time with a Double DDT. In June 2007 the Innovators beat Balls & Axl (Dreamer's Double DDT on Axl), the bWo (Cactus's Double Arm DDT on Stevie) and Paul London and Brian Kendrick, Cactus having been Super Kicked by Stevie in the car park; at Wrestlepalooza they lose the World Tag Team Championship Match to the Whole F**kin' Show and afterwards ask Heyman for the Dudleys. In July the Dudleys beat them for the number one contendership with Big Dick Dudley Jr.'s and Daizy's help, after attacking them with chairs and a 3D through a table; at Summer Assylum the Innovators DDT the champions after the Tables Match and are floored by Ultimo Dudley II, they lose to the champions in a non-title match on Blood, Sweat and Beers, and in August they DDT the whole second generation and challenge the Dudleys for the Dudleyville Hardcore Titles at Heatwave. In August 2007 they beat the bWo (a Double DDT on Hollywood Nova) on Revolution and Big Dick Jr. and Ultimo Dudley II (a Double DDT on Ultimo Dudley II) on Blood, Sweat and Beers, and after the Dudley Boyz beat the Briscoe Boys they cane the second generation of Dudleyz, DDT Bubba Ray and D-Von and take the Dudleyville Hardcore Title belts with them. At Heatwave they win the titles from the Dudley Boyz, whom they put through a table with a Double DDT, and the Whole F**kin' Show attack them afterwards; the diary then calls the belts the ECW Hardcore Tag Team Championship, 'newly rechristened'. In September, with Beulah McGillicutty at their side, the Innovators ask the World Tag Team Champions for a Champions versus Champions match at Anarchy Rulz to crown the Undisputed Tag Team Champions, and Tommy Dreamer pins Rob Van Dam on Revolution when Shawn Michaels's Super Kick misses Dreamer and hits Van Dam. At Anarchy Rulz in September 2007 they lose the Champions versus Champions match by a no contest when the Dudley Family run in; Tommy Dreamer is pinned by D-Von on Blood, Sweat and Beers. In October, with Beulah McGillicutty at their side, they ask Paul Heyman for a Singapore Cane Match, Dreamer's DDT beats Ultimo Dudley II, and at Guilty As Charged Cactus Jack and Dreamer are eliminated in the Three Way Dance (Bubba Ray pins Dreamer after Michaels's Sweet Chin Music and Cactus Jack after the Whole F**kin' Show's 420 Splash through a table), losing the Dudleyville belts, but they leave with all four tag belts and beat the second generation of Dudleyz with a Double DDT the next night before taking the belts from ringside again. In November 2007 the Innovators carry all four tag belts to the ring and beat Brandon Thomaselli with a Double DDT on Blood, Sweat and Beers; Tommy Dreamer and Cactus Jack say that at November To Remember XV they will win both tag titles and leave as the first Undisputed ECW Tag Team Champions, and Paul Heyman books the match against the Dudley Boyz to unify the titles. They beat the Second Generation of Dudleyz with a Double DDT on the last Revolution before the pay-per-view, and join the eight-man brawl that ends that show with Singapore canes. At November To Remember XV the Innovators come to the ring with Singapore canes and lose to the Dudley Boyz, Tommy Dreamer taking a Dudley Death Drop through a flaming table while Cactus Jack and Beulah McGillicutty lie beaten; the Dudley Boyz raise the Undisputed ECW Tag Team Titles. Cactus Jack's promo that night accuses Nate Hatred of maiming the men who paved the way for him and warns that 'when you insult one Hardcore Innovator, you insult them both'. Dreamer loses his Masters of Pain qualifying match to Chris Hero on the Saturday show when Hatred knocks him out with a Decapitator Lariat; on Revolution on the first Monday of December Cactus Jack is ruled knocked out in his qualifier with Mark Calaway after Hatred hits both men with Decapitator Lariats, and Hatred floors both Innovators with a Double Decapitator. On the Saturday show Hatred beats Dreamer, and James Mitchell books a handicap match against both at Got Blood?; Cactus's promo calls himself 'the cripple' who 'actually enjoys that pain'.

name: Team England

tenures.source: The diary's own posts bill the group; its first mention is at /promotions/ecw-worldwide-nevermore/archive/month-2007-06-p967-1005.html.

caption: The England squad for ECW's Wrestling World Cup in July 2007, announced in June 2007: Steven Regal, released from his Federation contract, introduces himself as its active team captain and recruits Paul Burchill, who agrees, and the developmental talents Nigel McGuinness and Doug Williams. Williams and McGuinness come out with steel chairs to even the numbers against Raven's Nest on Revolution, lose to CM Punk and Vito on Blood, Sweat and Beers and, after a no contest on Burchill's match, lose again to Vito and Monsters Inc on the next Revolution. In the World Cup of July 2007 England win the first Pool B match, over India, lose to Mexico twice and to India once (Raven and Punk distract Paul Burchill), and scrape into the quarter-finals one point ahead of India; they beat Team USA when Burchill beats Jay Briscoe, Christopher Daniels and Jerry Lynn after Kurt Angle's punch, beat Mexico when Burchill beats Rey Mysterio Jr. and Eddie Guerrero with a Double C-4, and win the first Wrestling World Cup at Summer Assylum when Burchill, last of the three left, beats Masato Tanaka, Jushin Lyger and Ultimo Dragon; Paul Heyman presents the trophy. Davey Boy Smith is on the squad throughout.

name: Team Canada

tenures.source: The diary's own posts bill the group; its first mention is at /promotions/ecw-worldwide-nevermore/archive/month-2007-06-p967-1005.html.

caption: The Canadian squad for the Wrestling World Cup, announced on Blood, Sweat and Beers in June 2007 by Don Callis, who has taken a leave from the Revolution announce desk to coach it: Lance Storm, Chris Benoit, Christian, Chris Jericho, Teddy Hart and Bobby Roode, with Christian and Jericho carrying Canadian flags to the ring. Joey Styles asks why Bret and Owen Hart were not picked, and Taz answers that they have their title business and do not see eye to eye. Canada beat Scotland twice and Japan once, tie Japan on points and lose the random draw for first place in Pool C, and are eliminated by Mexico in the quarter-final; Christian, whose last match is the pool win over Scotland, then leaves ECW for the WWA.

identity.note: An exact name match with another promotion's own group. Each is filed as its own per-promotion row, never merged.

name: Team USA

tenures.source: The diary's own posts bill the group; its first mention is at /promotions/ecw-worldwide-nevermore/archive/month-2007-06-p1006-1033.html.

caption: The American squad for ECW's Wrestling World Cup of July 2007, introduced on Revolution in June with Kurt Angle, on crutches, as coach and Jerry Lynn, Paul London, Brian Kendrick and the Briscoe brothers as the squad; Christopher Daniels earns the last place by beating Chris Hero at Wrestlepalooza. The Americans win all four Pool A matches, over the sWo (twice) and over Italy (twice), and finish top of the pool; in the quarter-final against England they lead three to one until Angle jumps Lynn from the apron in the last match, after which Paul Burchill's C-4 and Standing Shooting Star Press eliminate the team. Angle's excuse, a 'Subconscious Independent Retribution Therapy' brought on by post-traumatic stress, is called a lie by Lynn, and Chris Hero tells Angle in a backstage scene that the two had worked the angle together.

name: Team Scotland

tenures.source: The diary's own posts bill the group; its first mention is at /promotions/ecw-worldwide-nevermore/archive/month-2007-06-p1006-1033.html.

caption: The Scottish squad for the Wrestling World Cup of July 2007, introduced on Revolution in June with White Tiger as captain beside Drew Galloway, Drew McDonald and Eric Canyon. Drawn into Pool C with Japan and Canada, they are beaten in all four of their pool matches, by Canada twice and by Japan twice, and finish bottom of the pool.

name: Team Ireland

tenures.source: The diary's own posts bill the group; its first mention is at /promotions/ecw-worldwide-nevermore/archive/month-2007-06-p1006-1033.html.

caption: The Irish squad for the Wrestling World Cup of July 2007, introduced on Revolution in June with Fit Finlay as captain beside Sheamus O'Shaunnessy, Red Vinny and Blake Norton. In Pool D with Samoa and Puerto Rico they win one and lose one against each, and, level on eight points with Puerto Rico, qualify for the quarter-finals on falls scored; Japan eliminate them in the quarter-final.

name: Team Samoa

tenures.source: The diary's own posts bill the group; its first mention is at /promotions/ecw-worldwide-nevermore/archive/month-2007-06-p1006-1033.html.

caption: The Samoan squad for the Wrestling World Cup of July 2007, introduced on Revolution in June with Sika as coach and Ekmo, Anoai, Afa and Jo as the squad; on the screen the three brothers fight as the Samoan Gangstas, with their Samoan Drive-By finish. They top Pool D on nine points, thanks to the bonus point against Puerto Rico, and are eliminated in the quarter-final by the sWo, whose interference decides the match; in August the Samoan Gangstas lose to Balls & Axl and Afa attacks Brandon Thomaselli.

name: Team Puerto Rico

tenures.source: The diary's own posts bill the group; its first mention is at /promotions/ecw-worldwide-nevermore/archive/month-2007-06-p1006-1033.html.

caption: The Puerto Rican squad for the Wrestling World Cup of July 2007, introduced on Revolution in June with the brothers Carly and Eddie Colon as captains beside Jeff Jeffrey, Chicano and Apolo. In Pool D they lose to Ireland, beat Samoa, beat Ireland and lose to Samoa, which gives Samoa the bonus point; they finish level with Ireland on eight points and are eliminated on falls scored.

name: Team Italy

tenures.source: The diary's own posts bill the group; its first mention is at /promotions/ecw-worldwide-nevermore/archive/month-2007-06-p1006-1033.html.

caption: The Italian squad for the Wrestling World Cup of July 2007, introduced on Revolution in June with Little Guido as captain beside Tony Mamaluke and Sal E Graziano (the diary's Big Sal). In Pool A they beat the sWo once, lose to them once and twice to Team USA, and are knocked out when the sWo take the match that would have kept them in the race and Cuervo's spray paint helps Team USA beat them in the last round.

name: Team India

tenures.source: The diary's own posts bill the group; its first mention is at /promotions/ecw-worldwide-nevermore/archive/month-2007-06-p1006-1033.html.

caption: The Indian squad for the Wrestling World Cup of July 2007, introduced on Revolution in June with Sabu as captain beside the Headhunters and Sonjay Dutt. Sabu, the 'Bombay native' from Bombay, Michigan, wrecks opponents with chairs, and India beat England once but lose to England and twice to Mexico, and are knocked out by a single point; Sabu destroys the ringside after the last match.

name: The Dudley Family

tenures.source: The diary's own posts bill the group; its first mention is at /promotions/ecw-worldwide-nevermore/archive/month-2007-07-p1065-1139.html.

caption: The 'first family of Dudleyville': Bubba Ray and D-Von Dudley, who introduce their 'second generation' on Revolution in July 2007, Big Dick Dudley Jr. and Daizy Dudley, the 'nephew' and 'niece' of the Dudley Boyz and children of the missing Big Dick Dudley, and at Summer Assylum a third, Ultimo Dudley II. With the second generation at ringside the Dudleys win the number one contendership, lose the Tables Match at Summer Assylum to the Whole F**kin' Show, rename the old World Tag Team belts the Dudleyville Hardcore Titles, and defend them against the bWo, Balls & Axl and, on the previews, Los Guerreros and the Hardcore Innovators. In August 2007 the family (Bubba Ray, D-Von, Daizy, Big Dick Dudley Jr. and Ultimo Dudley II) interfere in the Dudleyz's title defences and lose a match to the Hardcore Innovators on Blood, Sweat and Beers when Ultimo Dudley II is pinned after a Double DDT; at Heatwave they tell the Innovators in a backstage promo the story of Big Daddy Dudley's grizzly bear and the table, before the Dudleyz lose the belts. In September they beat the Briscoe Boys, the F.B.I. and the Headhunters on F' The Mainstream and lose to the bWo, Daizy beats Traci in a catfight match when Big Dick Jr. hits her with a Total Penetration Chokebomb, Kelly Thomaselli beats Daizy to qualify for the Lioness' Den, and an unnamed Dudley, Slyk Tayshaun Dudley, a son of Big Dick Dudley, attacks the family with a chair and a flagpole, saying D-Von knows a secret that made his father leave, until the family beat him and put him through a table. At Anarchy Rulz in September 2007 the family run in on the Champions versus Champions match and carry off both sets of belts. In October they ask Paul Heyman for a Flaming Tables Match, Big Dick Jr. and Ultimo Dudley II lose to the Whole F**kin' Show and to the Hardcore Innovators (Dreamer's DDT on Ultimo Dudley II), Big Dick Jr. is pinned by Shawn Michaels and by Slyk Tayshaun Dudley, who kicks him low after calling out 'is that Big Dick?', and at Guilty As Charged they help the Dudley Boyz win the Three Way Dance before the Innovators leave them laid out backstage and take the belts. In November 2007 Daizy tells the Hardcore Innovators that the belts they carry belong to her uncles, and the family run out to the Innovators after they beat the Thomaselli brothers, until Slyk Tayshaun Dudley, a cousin who calls them a disgrace, chairs Daizy, Big Dick Jr. and Ultimo Dudley II and then Bubba Ray and D-Von, and says that he is entering the International All Action Title Tournament and means to find out the secret his father kept. He beats Scorpio Sky after the Second Generation run in and are chaired, clears the family again when the Second Generation lose to the Innovators with a Double DDT on Revolution, and on the last Revolution before the pay-per-view takes a five-on-one beating from the whole family until the Innovators arrive with Singapore canes. At November To Remember XV Big Dick Jr. costs his cousin Slyk Tayshaun Dudley the International All Action Championship with a Total Penetration, and Daizy and D-Von tell the camera that the family will 'take out the Hardcore Innovators'; Slyk then batters every one of his relatives, even Daizy, with a baseball bat and says that he will find out the secret about his father. On the Saturday show Ultimo Dudley II trips Slyk into Dick Jr.'s Total Penetration through a table, and Dick wins the falls-count-anywhere match. On Revolution on the first Monday of December Slyk interrupts his uncles' title defence with the bat, Dick Jr. blocks it with a chair, and in the restarted Three Way Dance Slyk and Dick Jr. win the Undisputed ECW Tag Team Titles; on Saturday Slyk, in a backstage scene, asks Dick Jr. and Daizy to join him in finding the family secret, with the belts as leverage, and the new champions beat the Thomasellis with Daizy's help before the Original Dudleyz (Bubba Ray, D-Von and Ultimo Dudley II) destroy the brothers.

name: The Samoan Gangstas

tenures.source: The diary's own posts bill the group; its first mention is at /promotions/ecw-worldwide-nevermore/archive/month-2007-08-p1177-1203.html.

caption: The three Samoan brothers of Team Samoa, Ekmo, Anoai and Afa, who fight on the screen as a team after the World Cup of July 2007, finishing with the Samoan Drive-By. In August 2007 they are the challengers on Blood, Sweat and Beers for the Dudleyville Hardcore Titles and lose when the Dudley Boyz pin Anoai with a 3D after the second generation of Dudleyz weighs in; on F' The Mainstream in September they beat the Headhunters (Ekmo pins Headhunter A with a Flying Splash), the Briscoe Boys (the Samoan Drive-By) and the F.B.I. (the Samoan Drive-By again).

name: The True World Order

tenures.source: The diary's own posts bill the group; its first mention is at /promotions/ecw-worldwide-nevermore/archive/ppv-guilty-as-charged-p1535-1562.html.

caption: Big Stevie Cool and The Great Sasuke, who turn on their own groups at Guilty As Charged in October 2007: when the bWo and the sWo meet in an eight-man tag with the loser to disband, Big Stevie Cool Stevie Kicks Hollywood Nova, BW Snow and Ozz after Sasuke has pinned Nova, Sasuke Superkicks Chessman, and Stevie says that he was the masked 'mole' who had been attacking the bWo, that the two of them are 'the only respectable wrestlers in this whole bunch', that the angle is 'a parody of a parody' and that they are 'the TRUE World Order'. The diary's previews bill them as Stevie Richards and The Great Sasuke; they make their debut as a team on Blood, Sweat and Beers against London and Kendrick and win when Sasuke hits a Michinoku Driver on Kendrick. In November 2007 Sasuke and Stevie Richards beat Mark Briscoe with a Michinoku Driver on Revolution; Stevie interferes against Rob Van Dam and Sasuke is pinned by Van Dam's 420 Splash, the two attack Shawn Michaels after he beats Sal Thomaselli until Van Dam saves him with a chair and the Van Daminator, and they lose to the Whole F**kin' Show on Revolution. On the Saturday show after November To Remember XV The Great Sasuke says that he was 'given f**king sWo angle' and 'stranded with face-paint Mexican freaks for a year', and loses to Juventud Guerrera's Juvi Driver; the F' The Mainstream recap has the True World Order beat 'Masked & Magnificent' in 8:43 after a Stevie Kick. On the Saturday show of the first week of December Sasuke loses to Rob Van Dam's Van Daminator in a Masters of Pain qualifier, and Stevie Richards, who calls Sasuke his new partner, is stopped by Shawn Michaels's Sweet Chin Music.

name: The New Extreme Order

tenures.source: The diary's own posts bill the group; its first mention is at /promotions/ecw-worldwide-nevermore/archive/month-2007-10-p1441-1534.html.

caption: Nate Hatred, Chris Hero and James Mitchell, whom the diary bills as 'The New Extreme Order' when they walk to the ring on Blood, Sweat and Beers in October 2007 (and calls 'The New Blood' in the match before). Hero helps Hatred beat Paul Burchill at Anarchy Rulz, with the Decapitator Lariat, and the Sinister Minister, Hero and Hatred celebrate with a hug; Hero costs Bret Hart his match with Hatred and, in a handicap match with Hatred, rolls Bret up with his feet on the ropes; Hatred beats Sabu on Blood, Sweat and Beers and on Revolution with Hero's help, and Mitchell challenges Sabu to a Streak versus Career Match at November To Remember XV. In November 2007 Nate Hatred, with James Mitchell, interferes in the Mark Calaway and Sabu match on Revolution, beats Calaway and Sabu with Rhino on Blood, Sweat and Beers, and has Mitchell promise Sabu his 'day of judgement' in the Streak versus Career Match at November To Remember XV; Hatred beats Brandon Thomaselli with the Decapitator Lariat, and after Sabu beats Masato Tanaka he wraps barbed wire round Sabu's neck and hangs him over the ropes, the broadcast cutting away, and on the last Revolution a mannequin of Hatred hangs from barbed wire and burns in a corridor. Chris Hero, who calls himself 'The Saviour of ECW', beats Chris Jericho twice in three nights, Jerry Lynn and Sal Thomaselli, and with Punk beats Jericho and Vito on Blood, Sweat and Beers. At November To Remember XV Nate Hatred, with James Mitchell, beats Sabu in the Streak versus Career Match with a Big Splash onto barbed wire and a Decapitator Lariat and spits at Sabu's offered hand, and Chris Hero beats Chris Jericho with Hero's Welcome after a Liontamer. On the Saturday show Hero beats Tommy Dreamer in a Masters of Pain qualifier when Hatred knocks Dreamer out; on Revolution on the first Monday of December Hatred and Mitchell break up Cactus Jack's qualifier with Mark Calaway, Hatred hitting both men with Decapitator Lariats so that Cactus is ruled knocked out, and he floors both Innovators with a Double Decapitator. On the Saturday show Hero beats Eddie Guerrero with Hero's Sidekick, and Hatred beats Dreamer; Mitchell announces a handicap match against both Innovators at Got Blood?, and Hatred smashes a microphone handle into his own forehead until he bleeds.
